A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LILO. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original optimization experiments across eight environments, including baseline comparisons and method ablations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original optimization experiments, including NAS-Bench-201, text summarization, preference-label accuracy, and additional ablations.

M1.justification: V2 adopts input-space-only GP modeling as its main formulation; v1 fitted input- and outcome-space GPs, although it already discussed omitting the latter. More substantially, v1's one-shot pair selection using the previous GP becomes sequential labeling with random initialization, qEUBO selection, and GP refitting between chunks (v2 Algorithm 2). Question generation also drops the preselected outcome indices.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original four outcome-function families and adds categorical architecture optimization on NAS-Bench-201 with Edge and Research personas. It also evaluates CNN/DailyMail summarization with generated text as outcomes (Section 5.3.5 and Appendix F.8), substantially extending domain and task coverage. Images are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: The four main baseline families remain; preferential BO is renamed preference BO. The matched feedback-acquisition comparison adds qPredES and separate batched and greedy EUBO entries (Table 2). The new summarization comparison includes random candidate acquisition alongside the quantitative BO baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds 16-trial evaluations and changes the feedback-budget study from matched budgets of 1, 2, or 4 to one LILO message versus up to 16 quantitative responses. The reported area-prior selection changes from the top 5% to 10%. Summarization introduces five-trial protocols using three fresh or ten fixed training articles and 20 held-out articles. DTLZ2's corrected main-text dimensions already appeared in v1's appendix.

E4.justification: The input-GP/outcome-GP/random pair-selection ablation is replaced by sequential qEUBO versus random labeling under restricted budgets. V2 expands feedback-budget analyses and adds direct label-accuracy measurement, longer-horizon evaluation, UCB and Thompson-sampling sensitivity, and fixed versus sampled article studies. The LLM-choice ablation is retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Figure 3 changes the reported replication count from 30 to 32 while retaining 95% confidence intervals; the scalar-versus-pairwise study changes from 30 to 16 replications per environment. The retained LLM ablation still reports 30. Some v2 counts are inconsistent: Table 2 says 30 while Appendix F.3 says 32, and Figure 15's caption and main-text footnote also disagree.

E6.justification: V2 revises benchmark curves and Table 2 and adds substantial NAS, summarization, labeling-budget, and longer-horizon results. Summarization matches the strongest oracle-feedback baselines, while longer runs sometimes let quantitative baselines overtake LILO. Figure 13 adds mean label accuracy of approximately 84% initially and 89% finally; F.4's above-90% description does not match the plotted means. V1 Table 1 is retained unchanged as v2 Table 3. Revised settings preclude treating all score differences as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds mathematical definitions for NAS utility, including sigmoid contributions, interactions, and penalties, and for summarization utility with weighted quality scores and a completion penalty (D.2 and F.8.2). Existing optimization and benchmark formulations remain. The added GP and EUBO background explains existing machinery; neither version supplies new theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims concerning language feedback, GP-guided optimization, sample efficiency, and textual priors remain. However, v1's conclusion claims successful application in multiple Meta A/B-testing campaigns; v2 replaces this with a belief that LILO suits such settings. Unstructured-output applicability becomes a listed contribution but was already asserted in v1 Section 1.1.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies feedback-efficiency comparisons by discussing unequal decision-maker workload and interprets eventual baseline overtaking through limitations of LLM in-context learning and convergence. It describes summarization as an initial illustration and explicitly identifies human evaluation as future work. Conversely, v1's warning about bias toward the LLM's own world knowledge is removed.

D1.justification: V2 supplies code-access information, specifies batched BoTorch acquisition implementations and categorical kernels, and documents new utility parameters, summarization protocols, algorithms, and prompts. These substantially expand reproducibility information. However, v1's disclosure of five LLM calls per labeling instance disappears without a replacement count; this omission does not establish an actual sampling change.

R1.justification: V2 adds Handa et al. as a language-based preference-elicitation comparison and references supporting the new benchmarks, metrics, and acquisition analyses. References to Alamdari, Ye, and Muller are removed. Appendix E's comparison table systematizes the existing positioning around feedback format, search space, LLM role, and uncertainty, while retaining the central novelty argument.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, baseline descriptions, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Related work and background become separate sections, experimental subsections are reordered, and the appendices are reorganized into dedicated implementation, baseline, environment, related-work, and results sections with a contents page. The title also drops Interactive.

P2.justification: V2 introduces a two-column main layout, redraws the overview graphics, and replaces Figure 2 with a different conceptual illustration. Benchmark panels are expanded and rearranged, the scalar ablation becomes a standalone figure, and numerous analytical plots and a related-work table are added. Existing appendix tables and conversation examples are also relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central mechanism and its applicability: previously untested textual outcomes receive a held-out summarization evaluation, preference-label accuracy is measured directly, and feedback-budget, acquisition, and longer-horizon studies expose both strengths and limits. Expanded reproducibility information and clearer organization further improve assessability. These gains outweigh reporting inconsistencies, including Table 2's conflicting counts and Figure 13's overstated accuracy description. Reliance on simulated decision makers remains an important limitation.
